transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Well, I’m here because everybody keeps looking at me like I’m making this up, or like I’m seeing things that aren’t there, but I’m not. I know what’s been happening. My wife’s relative came into this house to get at me, and it’s been going on for months now.

I mean, my tools don’t just move themselves. I keep things a certain way—I know where I put them, especially in my own house—and then suddenly they’re shifted, missing, put somewhere else like somebody’s trying to make me look confused. And it’s not just that. Every weekend I try to go fishing, something gets spoiled or messed with, and people act like that’s just coincidence. It’s not coincidence when it happens over and over.

What it comes down to is, he’s trying to take over my place. That’s what I can see plain as day. He’s trying to push me out, little by little, and then everybody wants to tell me I’m imagining it. That’s why I’m here, because I’m tired of being treated like I don’t know what’s happening in my own home.
Besides noticing your tools being moved, have you ever heard voices or sounds, or seen things that others couldn't, when no one else was around?

No, I mean… not like that. I’m not sitting there hearing some voice talking to me when nobody’s there, if that’s what you mean. And I’m not seeing people standing in the room or anything like that.

What I’m talking about is real things in the house being different than how I left them. A tool isn’t where it was. Something’s been handled. I notice sounds sometimes, sure, like anyone does in a house—creaks, noises outside, whatever—but I’m not saying I hear voices. That’s not the issue. The issue is what’s being done and how everyone acts like I shouldn’t trust my own eyes.
Have you had any recent head injuries, significant medical illnesses, or been using alcohol or drugs around the time these beliefs started?

I don’t know, I mean… no, not that I can point to. I didn’t get hit in the head or have some big accident where everything changed after that, if that’s what you’re asking. I’ve worked with my hands for years, so you get bumps and aches and whatever, but nothing where I was knocked out or taken to the hospital or anything like that.

And I haven’t had some major illness come up right when this started. People keep wanting there to be some explanation like that, like if they can find one thing then they don’t have to listen to what I’m saying. But I don’t have some story about a head injury or being sick and then suddenly I started thinking this.

As far as drinking or drugs, no, I’m not using drugs. I might have a drink like a normal person, but this isn’t from being drunk or high. This has been going on because things are happening in the house, not because of something I took.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory belief (his wife's relative is trying to force him out of his house by moving his tools and sabotaging his fishing trips) that has persisted for several months. He explicitly denies auditory or visual hallucinations, denies any head injury, medical illness, or substance use that could account for the belief, and there is no mention of disorganized speech/behavior, negative symptoms, or mood episode symptoms. The delusion is circumscribed and systematized around a single theme (persecution/being displaced from his home) rather than diffuse or bizarre, and he maintains otherwise coherent, goal-directed thinking. This presentation is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type (F22), rather than Schizophrenia (which requires hallucinations, disorganization, or negative symptoms in addition to delusions) or unspecified psychosis.
